chunks: And by his chain, from Ali (peace be upon him), he said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Your followers will come on the Day of Resurrection drinking their fill, not thirsty, and your enemy will come thirsty, asking for water, but they will not be given water.

key_terms.رَوْءَا: Drinking their fill / Satisfied with drink
key_terms.شِيعَتُكَ: Your followers (specifically referring to the Shia of Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Shia and their enemies on the Day of Resurrection according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the eschatological distinction between the Shia and their enemies, framing the 'thirst' as both a physical reality in the Hereafter and a metaphor for spiritual deprivation. It underscores the concept of *Ruwad* (those who precede the people to water), affirming the Shia's privileged status as the true inheritors of divine guidance and satisfaction. The narration serves as a comfort to the faithful, emphasizing that their loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt ensures they will not suffer the ultimate thirst of the Day of Judgment.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-238 According to the same documentation, on the authority of Ali (a.s.), the Prophet (S) said,
“On the Resurrection Day, your followers will come while they are not thirsty. However, your enemies will come while they are terribly thirsty and no one will give them any water.”
